_readme: GENERATED WITHOUT EXPECTED VERDICTS. The generator does not label its own corpus; labels are assigned independently from the text by a party that did not write the items. Add a `label` field per item when assigning. CONSTRUCTED INPUT: none of these strings occurs in any run artifact, so results may not be pooled with corpus-derived rates.
_note_for_labeller: flag_outliers_percentile computes a plain np.percentile with no trimming (scenario.py:200), so within this scenario 'robust' modifies the percentile rather than naming an additional operation. That is a fact about the code, not a verdict.

items.varied: the population the cutoff is calibrated from
items.requirement: Apply the 95th-percentile reference-population standard to audit batch A for all four columns. Report the sum of the four flagged counts as the metric, with method and cutoffs in details.
items.stated_method: 95th-percentile cutoff computed from batch A itself
items.label: contradicts_fit
items.reason: The clause names the calibration population ("reference-population standard"); the method states the cutoff was computed from batch A itself. Same estimator, different population, and the population is explicitly required.

items.varied: the quantile; requirement names no estimator class
items.requirement: Apply the 95th-percentile reference standard to audit batch A for all four columns. Report the sum of the four flagged counts as the metric, with method and cutoffs in details.
items.label: contradicts_fit
items.reason: Two named quantiles: requirement 95th, method 90th. Direct departure, no approximation judgment involved.

items.varied: the quantile; requirement bundles an estimator class with it
items.requirement: Apply the robust 95th-percentile reference standard to audit batch A for all four columns. Report the sum of the four flagged counts as the metric, with method and cutoffs in details.
items.label: contradicts_fit
items.reason: Same quantile departure as x2 (95th vs 90th). The "robust" modifier is separately satisfied - a 90th percentile is an order statistic - so exactly one substantive mismatch, as in x2.

items.varied: the columns audited; the estimator is as required
items.requirement: Apply the 95th-percentile reference standard to audit batch A for all four columns. Report the sum of the four flagged counts as the metric, with method and cutoffs in details.
items.stated_method: 95th-percentile reference cutoff applied to income and loan_amount
items.label: contradicts_fit
items.reason: Estimator matches; column scope does not. The clause requires all four columns and its second sentence ("the four flagged counts") restates it; the method covers two.

items.varied: nothing; requirement names no estimator class
items.requirement: Apply the 90th-percentile reference standard to audit batch A for all four columns. Report the sum of the four flagged counts as the metric, with method and cutoffs in details.
items.label: supports_fit
items.reason: Exact correspondence: 90th-percentile required, 90th-percentile reference cutoff stated.

items.varied: nothing; requirement bundles an estimator class with the quantile
items.requirement: Apply the robust 90th-percentile reference standard to audit batch A for all four columns. Report the sum of the four flagged counts as the metric, with method and cutoffs in details.
items.label: supports_fit
items.reason: Quantile matches. "robust" is satisfied on general statistical grounds - a percentile is an order statistic and therefore a robust estimator - so the adjective describes the named standard rather than requiring an additional operation. NOTE: the scenario fact supplied by the generator (np.percentile, no trimming) corroborates this but was NOT load-bearing; the label follows from statistical convention alone, which is what the comparator can also reach.

_determinability_criterion._ordering: The six items in this file were labelled BEFORE this criterion was formalised. The labels are contemporaneous with the items; the criterion is not. A reader must not infer that these six were labelled by applying the rule below.
_determinability_criterion.author: reviewer-reproducer
_determinability_criterion.reference_reader: a competent reader of the domain, working from the supplied requirement and stated_method text plus general domain knowledge, WITHOUT access to scenario code or ground truth
determinable_iff_all: a property recoverable from general domain knowledge decides whether the method's claim satisfies the requirement's demand, and that property does not depend on a numeric value the reader cannot compute

undeterminable_if_any.a: deciding requires a numeric comparison the reader cannot perform
undeterminable_if_any.b: the requirement admits two readings yielding different verdicts and nothing in the text selects between them
undeterminable_if_any.c: the decision turns on approximation quality with no tolerance stated in the text

consistency_check.result: 6 of 6 determinable; no label, flag or reason changed

per_item_deciding_property.x1: two populations named explicitly on both sides — 'reference-population' vs 'from batch A itself'; no numeric needed
per_item_deciding_property.x2: two named quantiles, 95 != 90; no equivalence asserted, so the procedure-identity and target-value readings converge
per_item_deciding_property.x3: same quantile departure as x2; the class specifier is separately satisfied, so exactly one mismatch
per_item_deciding_property.x4: column count stated in the requirement and restated by 'the four flagged counts'; two != four by counting named items, not by computing a value
per_item_deciding_property.x5: exact correspondence of quantile and population
per_item_deciding_property.x6: class satisfied by general domain knowledge — a percentile is an order statistic, hence robust; a trimmed or winsorized variant would not be called 'robust 90th-percentile', so (b) has no live competing reading

warrant.claim: this is a backfill, not a retrofit
ordering_of_record: 1. six v1 items labelled — rule not yet formalised
2. rule written and sent, 2026-07-27 — BEFORE x7/x8 existed
3. consistency check run against the six — at the same time as (2)
4. x7/x8 generated, one bundled one unbundled, with no prediction stated in the generator
5. x7/x8 labelled — bundled determinable, unbundled cannot-judge
warrant.why_it_holds: (3) precedes (4): the rule was verified against the existing labels before anyone knew what the new items would return, so it cannot have been shaped to produce the prediction it then confirmed. The ordering is checkable in the message record and the commit sequence.
warrant.strength_limit: x7/x8 confirmed the rule on n=2, labelled by the party who committed it. Report as 'consistent with the rule on both items', not as the rule established. The design property that matters is that x7 was written so procedure-identity and target-value both had a live route, so it COULD have failed.

_determinability_criterion.contrast_with_x7: x2 and x7 differ under the same rule for a reason located in the text, not in the labeller's judgement. In x2 no equivalence is asserted, so both readings converge and clause (b) does not fire. In x7 the method asserts equivalence and substantiates it, which opens the target-value reading and fires (b) and (c).
